key_insight: METTA separates rapid within-episode adaptation from long-range cross-episode task inference to make meta-reinforcement learning more scalable.
engineering_relevance: Linear-sequence neural memory and compact episode summaries offer an alternative to costly attention over full interaction histories.
method: Use causal neural memory for fine-grained within-episode adaptation.
Retain compact episode-level summaries for cross-episode task inference.
Enable test-time training to adapt to unseen tasks and task families.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 50% success on held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments and stronger performance than transformer baselines on long-context, sparse-reward PointMaze tasks.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify memory savings or test-time training overhead, leaving deployment costs uncertain.
paper_title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
